rendered: The premise does not hold: the authors did not strain the NiTi wires beyond 10%[1]. The Methods say so directly: Tensile deformations beyond 10% were not performed to avoid delamination of the coating from the wire surface.[2] The wires were pulled only to 5%[3] and 10%[4] strains. That ceiling was a limit set to protect the coating, not a target they exceeded: higher strain risked peeling the V2O5 film off the wire. The upper level was chosen because it would and 10%, which would sufficiently exceed the saturation crack[5] density reported for similar films, so the film would be strained past the point where further cracking stops.
